article.title: Ubiquitous
article.description: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.
article.content: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.

generated.caption:
Ever notice how some things just seem to be *everywhere*? 🌍 That's when you can use the word **ubiquitous** (yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs)! It means present or found everywhere. This formal word is perfect for IELTS essays!

Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.'

Save this for your next essay and follow @TheEnglishVault for daily lessons!
generated.script: Jab koi cheez everywhere ho, har jagah dikhe, toh uske liye best English word kya hai? Iska right word hai ubiquitous. Pronunciation hai yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Ubiquitous ka matlab hai jo cheez present ho, appearing ho, ya found ho everywhere. Basically, har jagah ho. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Matlab, modern life mein smartphones ab har jagah hain. Toh ab jab bhi koi cheez har jagah present hai, everywhere hai, toh use ubiquitous kaho. slides.body: The word 'ubiquitous' refers to something that is present, appearing, or found everywhere. This formal and academic term is commonly used in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays, especially when discussing technology or globalization. For example, we can say 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life' to convey how widespread they are. By using 'ubiquitous', you can add a touch of sophistication to your writing and effectively describe something that is everywhere.
